deviations.what: The rollout noun also has overview, list and show (read-only, /rollouts); seed has its own --force (overwrite variables that already exist, as seed-variables.sh), besides pause's --force over non-terminal runs; idle, plan and verify are viewer verbs and never write, so the rollout document records pause, seed, import, enable, resume and upgrade:<host> but not idle or verify (verify's output is the evidence)
deviations.reason: the CLI registry requires overview/list/show on every noun; seed's skip-existing is not a guard; viewer verbs cannot write the admin-only rollout document

deviations.what: import and enable keep the editor role; they record their step in the rollout document only when the token may write it (admin) and otherwise report record: {recorded: false} instead of failing
deviations.reason: the confirmed roles say editor while PUT /rollouts is admin; the operator runs rollouts with the admin token

deviations.what: After Codex review round 1: changing a machine's install section (add, change or remove) requires the admin role (other machine fields stay editor); the rollout document is written through new admin endpoints POST /rollouts/{id}/steps/{name} (atomic per-step merge, server-set applied_at) and POST /rollouts/{id}/snapshot (first wins, 409 snapshot_recorded); GET /runs gains optional since and cursor (paged by finish time) for verify; resume records resume_requested before resuming; upgrade records upgrade:<host> started (admin) before any command; an ssh address that starts with - or holds whitespace/control characters is refused
deviations.reason: Codex r1 findings: installer env injection through a newline, a viewer token could trigger upgrade, read-merge-write lost steps, verify read only 1000 failed runs, the resume boundary was recorded late; the address check closes an ssh option injection the review did not raise

deviations.what: Codex round 2 on the rollout CLI: resume_requested is first-wins (409 step_recorded); enable refuses when a snapshot rule is absent; the shared venv is read from ExecStart over D-Bus (busctl, exact argv) instead of parsing 'systemctl show' text; and every /rollouts write refuses (exit 2) on an API that predates the endpoints, with plan reporting the API version. The release that ships the rollout CLI (0.18.12) is therefore bootstrapped once by hand ('Bootstrapping the first release' in docs/operations/rollout.md); the first rollout fully through the CLI is the next release, which changes t7
deviations.reason: the live API (0.18.8) has no /rollouts endpoints, so pause and upgrade cannot record anything; Codex accepted either a bootstrap path on the old API or a documented hand bootstrap, and the hand bootstrap keeps the admin check unchanged

deviations.what: 0.18.13 (t7) went out with idle, pause, seed, import, enable, resume and verify through the released 0.18.13 'culture-rules rollout'; spark's upgrade ran through the CLI from branch rules/57-shared-venv-host (upgrade:spark recorded); orin, spark2 and thor were upgraded by hand with install.sh over their ssh aliases using the records' install flags, so their upgrade steps are not in /rollouts/0.18.13. verify passed: 4 nodes and the API on 0.18.13, 25 rules = snapshot + new rules, no no_builtin
deviations.reason: Two CLI defects surfaced on the first full CLI rollout (#57): shared_venv upgrade compared socket.gethostname() (spark-f8a9) with the record name spark and refused on spark; install_sh upgrade sshed to the record's address (a tailnet IP), which ~/.ssh/config's Host/User aliases do not cover (host key verification failed on orin and spark2, publickey denied on thor); address cannot become the alias because placement requires a LAN/tailnet address

deviations.what: Follow-up 0.18.14 (#57): machine install gains ssh_target (one word, admin-only, never starting with -), upgrade's ssh/scp target ahead of address; the shared-venv local-host check also accepts the local culture-rules-node.service running 'node run --host <name>' (ExecStart over D-Bus, as the venv). The four machine records get ssh_target = their ssh alias after the release
deviations.reason: Fixes the two #57 defects so the next release rolls out fully through the CLI
